name: When Sport Became History
description: The Olympic Games, boxing rings, cricket grounds and football pitches where a match carried the weight of politics, race and nations.

checkpoints.name: Games old and new
checkpoints.note: The ancient Olympic Games honoured the gods at Olympia, and a modern Games began in Athens in 1896. The Ashes began in 1882 and made cricket between England and Australia a national rivalry.

checkpoints.name: Sport under dictators and after
checkpoints.note: Bodyline made the Ashes bitter and Don Bradman's batting was its target. At the 1936 Berlin Olympics Jesse Owens won four gold medals. Jackie Robinson joined the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947, and London hosted the 1948 Games.

checkpoints.name: New heroes
checkpoints.note: Brazil built the Maracana for the 1950 World Cup, and Uruguay beat the hosts there. In 1960 Abebe Bikila ran the Rome Olympic marathon barefoot, and the first Paralympic Games were held. In 1968 athletes used the Mexico City podium for protest.

checkpoints.name: Spectacle and rivalry
checkpoints.note: Attackers killed members of the Israeli team at the 1972 Olympics. Billie Jean King won the Battle of the Sexes, and Muhammad Ali fought in the Rumble in the Jungle and the Thrilla in Manila. The 1980 and 1984 Games were hit by boycotts, and the Miracle on Ice stunned the Soviets.

checkpoints.name: Nations and icons
checkpoints.note: Diego Maradona took Argentina to the 1986 World Cup title. In 1995 South Africa hosted and won the Rugby World Cup, and Nelson Mandela used the occasion to bring a divided country together.
